description: The figure presents two horizontal bar charts, one for mBERT and one for XLM-R, each illustrating the percentage point difference in probing performance between evaluating a single layer (or the concatenation of all layers) and evaluating a weighted sum of all layers, with negative values indicating worse performance for the single-layer probe. In both charts, the x-axis lists layer indices from 0 (embedding layer) to 12, followed by “concat” (concatenation of all layers), while the y-axis shows “% point difference” ranging from -10 to 0, with gridlines at every 2 units. For mBERT (top chart, light blue bars), the embedding layer (0) shows the largest negative difference at approximately -10.5%, followed by layer 1 at ~-8.5%, layer 2 at ~-7.5%, layer 3 at ~-5.5%, layer 4 at ~-4.5%, and layer 5 at ~-2.5%; layers 6 through 11 show small negative differences near -1% or less, layer 12 is at ~-1.5%, and “concat” is slightly positive at ~+0.5%. For XLM-R (bottom chart, dark blue bars), the pattern is similar: layer 0 is ~-10%, layer 1 ~-9.5%, layer 2 ~-8.5%, layer 3 ~-6%, layer 4 ~-4%, layer 5 ~-2.5%, layers 6–8 are near -1%, layer 9 is slightly less negative, layers 10–11 are slightly positive (~+0.5%), layer 12 is near 0, and “concat” is ~+0.5%. Both models show that early layers (especially 0–3) perform substantially worse than the weighted sum, while later layers and concatenation approach or slightly exceed the weighted sum’s performance.
